learning_outcomes.text: Model vibrations in a concrete situation, analytically with a simple numerical model (using RdM7).
Identify the most suitable models for a given vibration situation.
Interpret the results of analytical calculations and numerical simulations.
Understand basic vibration phenomena: free vibrations, forced vibrations, resonance.
Handle different types of modeling of systems subjected to vibration: analytical (1DDL, 2DDL, 1D, E.F.).
Compare and criticize the validity of different possible models for the same system.
Apply all these concepts to a case study chosen personally by each student.

syllabus_topics: Sequence 1: Discrete systems with one degree of freedom
Equation of dynamics, free vibration (with initial conditions), natural frequency
Sequence 2: Discrete systems with 2 or more degrees of freedom
Coupled equations of dynamics, modal analysis
Sequence 3: One-dimensional continuous systems with some analytical solutions
Tension/compression vibrations of straight beams: equilibrium equations (with boundary conditions), eigenmodes
Transverse vibrations of beams: analysis of a simple solution (embedded-free)
Sequence 4: Energy methods to obtain approximate numerical solutions
Theorem of kinetic energy and mechanical energy applied to vibrations
Expression of the mechanical energy of elementary structures (mass, spring, beams)
Introduction to the Finite Element Method in the case of vibrations, and the nature of the approximations involved
Each student is free to choose a subject for study, and applies the proposed approach to his or her case study
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1*RAP1)/1, indicating that the assessment is based entirely on a report (RAP1).
